text:
Maya: Heads up, opened a docs PR: adding a small YAML example for retention policies on the audit-logs page + a safe curl example for exporting audit events as CSV. Asking for legal wording checks and a link/anchor fix.

Jon: Nice. Quick things I saw: the YAML example used `retention: permanent` which we shouldn't use. Also the curl sample posts a `--data` payload with `user_email: alice@example.com`  please scrub.

Maya: Yep will scrub. Draft YAML I put in the PR (still WIP):
```yaml
# example enterprise retention config (Hosted)
retention:
  default_days: 365
  max_days: 1095  # example only; contact account team
  policy: "auto-delete"
```
Is that OK to show as an example?

Priya: Suggest a tiny wording change: don't include `max_days` as a public limit. Use `example_max_days` or a comment that it's illustrative only. And add a line: "This is an example configuration for Hosted only. Dedicated/Private customers should consult their contract."

Raj: Legal note: change "auto-delete" to "time-based deletion" and drop any implication of guarantees. Proposed text: "Example: Hosted customers may configure time-based deletion. Default operational retention is 365 days; customers requiring different retention should contact their account team. Dedicated/Private retention is contractual." Also add: "Access controls: logs are encrypted at rest and access is limited via RBAC; access events are recorded."

Maya: Updated YAML to be purely illustrative and added Raj's wording in the paragraph. New YAML in PR:```yaml
# illustrative Hosted example only
retention_example:
  default_days: 365
  note: "illustrative; not a product guarantee"
```

Jon: Good. About the curl CSV export snippet: please show redaction and use `--header 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>'` rather than a token literal. Draft I added:```bash
curl -X GET 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/audit/exports?since=2024-01-01' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -o audit_export.csv
# downstream: redact emails before storing long-term
```
We should explicitly call out: "Do not store raw CSVs with PII in long-term logs."

Priya: Added the redaction callout and a short code sample (Python) demonstrating safe load+redact:```py
import csv
with open('audit_export.csv') as f:
    r = csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in r:
        row['user_email'] = '<redacted>'
        # process row safely
        print(row['event_type'])
```

Raj: Legal micro-asks: (1) Replace any "Hosted customers may configure" with "Hosted customers may request" unless the UI already supports the config. (2) For the curl example, add a short sentence: "Audit export endpoints are access-controlled; ensure least-privilege tokens are used."

Maya: We don't have a self-serve retention UI for Hosted yet, so changed wording to "request". Updated PR text accordingly.

DocsBot: automated: PR title matches content. Suggested linking: the export example should link to /docs/api/audit-export and the YAML example to /docs/admin/config-retention.

Jon: Small link fix: current PR points to /docs/admin/retention which is the old path; changed to /docs/admin/config-retention. I pushed that commit.

Priya: Can LegalBot mark ready for review? Also asking for localization check - the SOC 2 phrasing translated to EU pages should avoid implying jurisdictional guarantees.

LegalBot: automated: Flagged for legal review. @Raj added as reviewer. Note on localization: legal translations team will review any jurisdiction-specific phrasing.

Raj: Reviewing now. Minor tweak: rephrase "ensure least-privilege tokens are used" to "use least-privileged credentials and rotate keys regularly." Also approve the illustrative YAML change. No further legal holds.

Maya: Thanks all. I'll accept the suggested tweaks and merge once the translations team confirms they don't need alternate wording for EU pages.

Priya: After merge I'll also open a short PR to sync the internal example repo with these snippets.

Jon: LGTM. Thanks for keeping the examples redacted and clearly illustrative.

Maya: Merging after translations ack. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
